deities: Lord Hanuman (natural rock icon in the cave; the perennial stream falls on the idol)

history.dynasty: None (mythological site; age of the present structures unverified)
history.summary: Hanuman Dhara is the famous cave temple of Chitrakoot, on a hill about 3 km from Chitrakoot Ramghat (UP side, near Karwi). Its name comes from the 'dhara' - a perennial stream said to fall continuously on the tail/left arm of the Hanuman idol. Legend: after burning Lanka (Lanka dahan), Hanuman's tail still burned; Lord Rama shot an arrow into the mountain peak, releasing the cooling stream, and asked Hanuman to settle in the cave to protect Chitrakoot's devotees. The Hanuman icon is said to be naturally formed in the rock, not carved. About 360 steps (roughly a half-hour climb; a ropeway is now also available) lead to the cave, passing statues of Ram, Sita and Lakshman; a small Ram shrine and the Sita Rasoi structure stand nearby. A pilgrimage to Chitrakoot is traditionally considered incomplete without darshan here.

name: Hanuman Dhara Temple
town_description: Chitrakoot is an ancient pilgrimage region spread across the Uttar Pradesh-Madhya Pradesh border, sacred in the Ramayana as the place of Lord Rama's exile. Hanuman Dhara stands on the UP side near Karwi town, about 3 km from Ramghat on the Mandakini river.

travel.airport: Chitrakoot Airport (Karwi), about 10 km (verify); major connectivity via Prayagraj, about 130 km (verify).
travel.railway: Chitrakoot Dham Karvi railway station, then taxi/auto to the base of the hill.
travel.road: About 3 km from Chitrakoot Ramghat; a 360-step climb (about 30 minutes) or a ropeway reaches the cave temple.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Hanuman Jayanti is the peak festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily per BhaktiBharat (verify locally).
